audience.value: DSAI 5101 instructor grading against the Part A rubric, plus master's classmates who know ML basics but not this dataset or delivery platforms

communication_intent.value: Explain how accurately delivery time can be predicted at order time and what drives long deliveries, then persuade that a better estimate is not automatically a better promise; follow one real order (#85188) through the whole talk

audience_outcome.value: The audience can state the research question, trust the leakage-free time-split evaluation, remember MAE 6.5 min (3.1 closer than the app) and distance as the main driver, and understand why the app still makes better promises

core_message.value: At ordering, delivery time can be predicted to about 6.5 minutes and distance drives it, but a good promise needs more than an accurate number, and every minute cut from a promise lands on a rider

delivery_context.value: Primary: presenter-led 10-minute live class talk by three speakers plus 5-minute Q&A on Sun 22 Nov; the deck is imported into Canva and edited there. Secondary: backup slides to point at during Q&A

artifact_afterlife.value: Editable in Canva by three teammates; exported to PDF and PPTX, slides.pdf committed to the repo
